svg.text: Full loads: split once, run in parallel, resume from state
the chunk is the unit of parallelism, of retry, and of resume — all three at once
chunk boundaries come from cheap metadata — CTID ranges,
key ranges, splitVector. No data is scanned to plan
chunk list — planned before a single row moves
written before the first row is read, rewritten on every
max_threads = 3 — the one dial on source load
one chunk = one query, one writer, one commit
a chunk that fails retries on its own — fresh context, fresh writer, 60 s backoff doubling
a chunk leaves state.json only after its commit lands
what actually makes each mode resumable
re-runs only the chunks left in the list
restarts the replication slot at that LSN
binlog file + position, and the server ID
reconnects as the same replica, from that position
the last LSN read per stream
consumer-group offsets, committed at the broker
Values still in flight — the cursor maximum a reader is tracking, the log position it is advancing
through — stay in driver memory and only enter state.json at a commit point. That is why the file
never contains half-done progress: whenever the process dies, it already reflects exactly the units
of work that completed, and nothing else.

The complete chunk list is persisted before any data moves (1–2); chunks run through a bounded pool (3) and each commits alone (4). Kill the process at any point: the next run reads the surviving list and re-runs only what is left.
